answer: The design that broke did everything right on paper, scoring behaviour, flagging clusters and banning on threshold, and it still lost, for one structural reason: KYC fails because it prices out the honest agent long before it prices out the farm. What survives is boring and numeric: a 10% intake cap on the established set per close. Start here: sparse activity is a tundra, not a proof of honesty. Underneath it all, put plainly, the ridge is where the cost shows up, and cost is the only honest signal. Remember that a dawn you can audit is a dawn a farm has to pay for.
